## 4. Receipt Required Threshold — Corporate Card Transactions `NWP-POL-006-04`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-006-01:** this section applies only
to transactions on a Northwind Prairie Holdings, Inc. corporate card
issued under `NWP-POL-008`, and sets a materially **higher**
receipt-required threshold than the general out-of-pocket threshold in
`NWP-POL-006-01`, because corporate-card transactions are already
captured in the statement feed and only need supporting documentation
above a higher amount.

| Category | Receipt required above (USD) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | $75 |
| Ground transportation | $75 |
| Lodging | $0 (always required) |
| Office/general supplies | $75 |
| Other | $75 |

## 1. Receipt Required Threshold — General `NWP-POL-006-01`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-006-04:** this section sets the
receipt-required threshold for **out-of-pocket / reimbursement**
expenses; `NWP-POL-006-04` sets a materially **higher** threshold for
**corporate card** transactions, because corporate-card spend is already
captured in the monthly statement feed described in `NWP-POL-008`.

A receipt is required for any out-of-pocket expense above the following
per-category thresholds. Expenses at or below the threshold may be
submitted with a self-attestation in place of a receipt.

| Category | Receipt required above (USD) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | $25 |
| Ground transportation | $25 |
| Lodging | $0 (always required) |
| Office/general supplies | $25 |
| Other | $25 |

### 1.1 Acceptable Receipt Formats `NWP-POL-006-01.01`

Acceptable formats are a photographed or scanned itemized receipt, an
emailed vendor invoice, or a vendor-issued digital receipt. A credit card
statement line alone is not an acceptable substitute for a receipt.

## 3. Standard Meal Caps `NWP-POL-004-03`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-005-02:** this section covers an
employee's own solo meals while traveling (no client present) and uses
materially lower per-person caps with no documentation requirement beyond
a receipt; `NWP-POL-005-02` covers client-facing entertainment, uses
higher caps, and additionally requires recording the client's name and
business purpose.

| Meal | Cap (USD/person/day) |
| --- | --- |
| Breakfast | $18 |
| Lunch | $22 |
| Dinner | $45 |

### 3.1 Receipt Requirement `NWP-POL-004-03.01`

Receipts are required for any single meal above the general receipt
threshold set in `NWP-POL-006-01`. Below that threshold, a per-diem style
self-attestation is sufficient.

## 2. Missing Receipt Affidavit `NWP-POL-006-02`

When a required receipt is lost, the employee may submit a missing
receipt affidavit describing the expense, in lieu of the receipt, no
more than twice per rolling 12-month period. A third or subsequent
missing-receipt affidavit in the same period requires `Department
Manager` approval.

## 3. Claim Process `NWP-POL-009-03`

Monthly stipend amounts (internet, utilities) are claimed through the
standard expense report process and do not require a receipt below the
general threshold set in `NWP-POL-006-01`. The one-time equipment cap
always requires an itemized receipt regardless of amount.

## 3. Approval Thresholds — International Travel and Relocation Spend `NWP-POL-007-03`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-007-01:** this section applies only
to spend under `NWP-POL-011` (International Travel Policy) and
`NWP-POL-010` (Relocation Policy), and requires **dual** sign-off at its
top tier — both `Department Manager` AND `Finance Admin` — rather than
the single `Finance Admin` sign-off that `NWP-POL-007-01` requires at the
equivalent tier for ordinary domestic spend.

| Report total | Required approval |
| --- | --- |
| Up to $500 | `Department Manager` |
| $500.01 – $5,000 | `Department Manager`, then `Finance Admin` |
| Above $5,000 | `Department Manager` AND `Finance Admin` (dual sign-off) |

## 3. Retention `NWP-POL-006-03`

Original receipts (paper or digital) should be retained by the employee
for 90 days after report approval, in case of an audit sampling review
under `NWP-POL-012-03`.

**Material difference from NWP-POL-007-03:** this section sets the
approval chain for ordinary domestic business expense, and its top tier

international travel and relocation spend and requires **dual** sign-off
(`Department Manager` AND `Finance Admin`) at the equivalent top tier,
reflecting the higher risk of that spend category.

| Report total | Required approval |
| --- | --- |
| Up to $500 | `Department Manager` |
| $500.01 – $5,000 | `Department Manager`, then `Finance Admin` |
| Above $5,000 | `Finance Admin` (single sign-off) |

### 1.1 Self-Approval Prohibition `NWP-POL-007-01.01`

No employee may approve their own expense report, regardless of role or
report total. A report submitted by a `Department Manager` routes to
another `Department Manager` or directly to `Finance Admin`.

## 5. Expense Report Submission Deadline — Current `NWP-POL-012-05`

**Status: CURRENT — replaces NWP-POL-012-02 effective 2024-06-01.**

Effective date: 2024-06-01.

Employees must submit expense reports within **30 calendar days** of the
date the expense was incurred. This rule supersedes the prior 60-day
deadline in `NWP-POL-012-02` effective 2024-06-01. Reports submitted
after 30 days require `Department Manager` approval to process; reports
submitted after 60 days additionally require `Finance Admin` approval
and may be denied at `Finance Admin` discretion.

The deadline was shortened from 60 to 30 days to align expense
recognition more closely with the monthly close process described
elsewhere in Northwind Prairie Holdings, Inc.'s (fictional) internal
finance calendar.

## 3. Approval `NWP-POL-010-03`

All relocation reimbursement requires the dual sign-off described in
`NWP-POL-007-03`, regardless of amount, due to the size and one-time
nature of relocation spend.

question: If I drive my own car to a client site, how much does the company pay me back per mile?

results.text:
## 2. Personal Vehicle Mileage Reimbursement `NWP-POL-001-02`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-010-02:** this section governs
per-mile reimbursement for routine business travel; `NWP-POL-010-02`
governs a one-time relocation moving-distance reimbursement and uses a
flat tier structure rather than a per-mile rate.

Employees who use a personal vehicle for approved business travel are
reimbursed per mile driven, at a rate that varies by vehicle class. The
standard mileage rate is reviewed annually and may be adjusted to track
published fuel-cost indices.

| Vehicle class | Rate (USD/mile) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard passenger vehicle | $0.67 | Default rate for sedans, hatchbacks, standard SUVs |
| Hybrid or electric vehicle | $0.70 | Incentive rate to encourage lower-emission travel |
| Motorcycle | $0.35 | |
| Personal vehicle towing equipment/trailer | $0.75 | Requires prior `Department Manager` approval |

Mileage is calculated from the employee's regular worksite to the
business destination, net of the employee's normal commute distance.
Commute-distance deduction does not apply on weekends or company
holidays.

### 2.1 Odometer and Mapping Evidence `NWP-POL-001-02.01`

Mileage claims must be supported by either odometer readings at
departure and arrival, or a mapping-service (routed-distance) printout.
Estimated or rounded mileage without supporting evidence is not
reimbursable.

## 2. Client Entertainment Per-Person Caps `NWP-POL-005-02`

**Material difference from NWP-POL-004-03:** this section covers
client-facing meals/entertainment and permits materially higher
per-person caps than the solo-employee meal caps in `NWP-POL-004-03`,
because client entertainment additionally requires recording the
client's name, company, and business purpose in the expense report — a
documentation requirement `NWP-POL-004-03` does not carry.

| Event type | Cap (USD/person) |
| --- | --- |
| Client meal (breakfast/lunch) | $60 |
| Client meal (dinner) | $110 |
| Client event/tickets (sporting, theater, etc.) | $150 |

Caps apply per person, per event, inclusive of tax and gratuity. A
moderate amount of alcohol is reimbursable under this policy when
consumed with a client meal, unlike under `NWP-POL-004`.

### 2.1 Required Documentation `NWP-POL-005-02.01`

Every client entertainment expense must record, in the expense report
notes field: the client's full name, the client's company, and a
one-sentence business purpose. Claims missing any of these three fields
are returned to the submitting employee for correction before approval.

## 2. Relocation Reimbursement Caps by Move Distance `NWP-POL-010-02`

flat one-time reimbursement tier for a full household relocation, unlike

rate rather than a flat move-distance tier.

| Move distance | Reimbursement cap (USD) |
| --- | --- |
| 50–199 miles | $3,000 |
| 200–999 miles | $7,500 |
| 1,000 miles or more | $12,000 |

Caps cover moving-company or truck-rental costs, temporary lodging up to
14 nights, and standard packing materials. They do not cover real estate
commissions or lease-break penalties.

An employee who voluntarily resigns within 12 months of a
company-funded relocation must repay the relocation reimbursement on a
prorated basis, per the repayment schedule in the employee's relocation
agreement.

This policy sets reimbursement caps for an employee's own meals while
traveling on approved business activity, **when no client, prospect, or

are governed by `NWP-POL-005` (Client Entertainment Policy), not this
document.

## 4. Rideshare, Taxi, Parking, and Tolls `NWP-POL-001-04`

Rideshare and taxi fares are reimbursable for business travel when more
cost-effective than a rental vehicle or when driving is impractical.
Parking and toll charges incurred during approved business travel are
fully reimbursable with receipt, regardless of amount, per the
documentation thresholds in `NWP-POL-006`.

## 3. Rental Vehicles `NWP-POL-001-03`

Rental vehicles may be used in place of personal-vehicle mileage when
total round-trip mileage exceeds 150 miles, or when a personal vehicle is
unavailable. Rentals must be booked in the economy or standard class
unless three or more employees are traveling together, in which case a
mid-size or larger vehicle may be booked.

### 3.1 Insurance `NWP-POL-001-03.01`

Employees must decline the rental company's supplemental insurance for
domestic travel, since Northwind Prairie Holdings, Inc. carries a
corporate policy covering rental vehicles used for business purposes.

## 2. General Rules `NWP-POL-004-02`

Meal caps apply per person, per day, and are inclusive of tax and
gratuity. Alcohol is not reimbursable under this policy. Meals are only
reimbursable on days that include overnight travel or travel exceeding
50 miles from the employee's regular worksite.

Per diem covers meals and incidentals only; lodging is booked and

| --- | --- | --- |
